reference.title: Band Skull Crusher
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the hands lower toward the forehead, exhale as the elbows straighten against the band.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: pick a band you can control for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: More reps, then a heavier band or a step farther from the anchor

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench with the head toward a rack; a band looped round both uprights behind you, a handle in each hand, arms straight up over the shoulders.
Breathe in and bend only the elbows; the band draws the hands back toward the forehead.
Hands just above the forehead, upper arms still, elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows against the band, moving only the forearms.
Arms straight but not locked over the shoulders; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging back and forth (turning it into a pullover)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling; only the forearms move.
Keep the elbows about shoulder width apart.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the hands back
mistakes.fix: Lower under control against the band; stop just above the forehead.

mistakes.mistake: Lower back arching off the bench
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep the feet planted and the ribs down.
Keep the wrists straight and the handles in the fingers and palm.

kinematics.norm: About shoulder width or a little narrower (clinical opinion)

Straight but not locked at the top; lower until the hands are just above the forehead, about 100-120 degrees of elbow flexion (clinical opinion). Activation and relative force were matched across the three heads at 90 degrees of flexion or more (PLoS ONE 2021)
Upper arms about vertical (about 90 degrees of shoulder flexion) and still; at 90 degrees and above the medial head carries the most force (Kholinne 2018)

Anchored behind the head so the band pulls the hands back toward the head and resists elbow extension; the strands must clear the head (clinical opinion). Elastic resistance gives similar muscle activation to free weights at matched effort (Andersen 2010)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s lowering and 1-1.5 s pressing (clinical opinion); the EMG comparison used sets of 7 reps at 70% of 1RM (Boehler 2011)

sources.title: GymVisual 14725, Band Skull Crusher, video (movement reference)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)
Effect of elbow joint angles on electromyographic activity versus force relationships of synergistic muscles of the triceps brachii (PLoS ONE 2021; PMC8174684)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjørnlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks and anchor it securely round the uprights before each set; a snapping band can hit the face.
Elbow pain: shorten the range or use a lighter band (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort: palms facing each other on the handles.
Elbow discomfort: lower only to the top of the head (less elbow bend).
progressions: Pause just above the forehead (1 s).

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Does all of the work: lowers the hands under control against the band and straightens the elbows. In the lying barbell triceps extension the long and lateral heads differed in activity (Boehler 2011). With the upper arm vertical the medial head produced the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Does all of the work: lowers the hands under control against the band and straightens the elbows. In the lying barbell triceps extension the long and lateral heads differed in activity (Boehler 2011). With the upper arm vertical the medial head produced the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Hold the upper arms vertical as the band pulls the hands toward the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Hold the upper arms vertical as the band pulls the hands toward the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps the lats keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps the lats keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the lower back from arching off the bench.
